The illustrious Bhairava said:
Aiṃ! O Goddess Mālinī, may you be victorious; you are the destroyer of stainless impurities.
You are the Goddess who has arisen as the power of knowledge (jñānaśakti), and you are the intellect that increases splendor.
The mother of all beings is established in this saṃsāra;
O Goddess Vīrāvalī, O affectionate one, show compassion!

Victorious is she who is born from the manifestation of the supreme reality and Nirvāṇa, consisting of radiant splendor; you are the Supreme Power of Ignorance (Māyā) who has emerged in manifest form, auspicious through her powers of Will and Action. You are the straight line, the beautiful stroke, appearing before us in the form of a coil like a sleeping serpent-king; you are celebrated as the Lordly Power of Sound (Nāda).

You are of the nature of radiant light, whose own form is auspicious (*śivā*), and you bear the names Śivā-jyeṣṭhā, Vāmā, Raudrī, and Ambikā known as Manā; you are the form of the *bindu*, the *avadhūtī*, and the shape of the half-moon; you are the triangle, the syllable *a*, the syllable *u-ma*, the syllable *ī*, and the syllable *o* joined together.

She whose nature is the letter *ka*, who abides in the form of the *bhaga* (the womb/vulva), who from the beginning arises from the reality of *kṣānti*, who is the form of the *yoni*, the awakener of Śrīkaṇṭha, the mother of Rudra,
likewise possessed of infinite power, most subtle, the immortal one of the three forms, the bearer of the arrow, the bearer of the burden, and the lunar day (*tithi*).

O Bhairavī, you who consist of Śātmikā, Aṣṭāṇubhūtā, and Hārā, and who are Jhaṇṭhīśa; you who are Sadyojāta-natured and worshipped for grace; you who consort with Krūra, Sāṅga, and Mahāsena; you who are the sixteen-fold nectar at the end, the mass of the *bindu*, and immersed in the body of vibration (*spanda*); you who bestow the bliss of the supreme *nirvāṇa* of the complete remainder—salutations to you!
She who possesses the power for play in the garden of Bhairava; the supreme destroyer; the power of Rudra; Khagī; Siddhiyogeśvarī;

the pervasive Mother of Siddhis; the mass of sounds; the ocean of the womb-syllables; the pure speech; Śivā; the Mistress of Speech of the Siddhas; Mātṛkā; the desire for the perfection of speech; Maṅgalā; Siddhilakṣmī; and Vibhūti.
She is the source, the goal, known as Śātā, Nārāyaṇī, Raktacaṇḍā, and Karālā; she possesses a terrifying form in the Mahocchuṣma-yoga, and through her beloved state,
she is Jayantī, the unconquered, and the deluder of Rudra— she who is called Navātmā, the deity.

O Goddess, you who possess a skull-bowl, a skeleton, and a skull-topped staff, are worshipped by mantra-following practitioners who recline upon the laps of their consorts, who are devoted to the drinking of heroes (vīrapāna), and who are deeply faithful, with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) during festivals of divine libations.
O you who delight in wine and meat, may you be satiated by those auspicious Śaiva and human beings— born of one, two, three, four, five, six, or seven births—
who shine with mantras, vidyās, and vows, and who follow the divine conduct as muṇḍas, kāpālikas, and kāpālins.

[Accompanied] by those who utter these mantra-syllables— *namaskāra*, *oṃkāra*, *svāhā*, *svadhākāra*, *vauṣaṭ*, *vaṣaṭkāra*, *hūṃkāra*, and *phaṭkāra*— by practitioners (*sādhaka*) and spiritual sons (*putraka*) holding rosaries in their left hands and reciting them, by Mothers (*mātṛ*), by mandalas, by the initiated, by yogins, and by the host of yoginīs;
O Goddess, you who bestow the yoga-perfections of the Yoginīs, you are worshipped by Rudras who delight in the play of the *melāpaka*;

with eyes as broad as lotus petals and filled with affection, you look upon him. Abiding in the divine celestial realm, you who move through the seven netherworlds, his unimpeded supernatural power (*siddhi*) is described by the waters of his devotion.

A pure-minded human being who recites this *Daṇḍaka* once, twice, thrice, or four, five, six, seven, or eight times a day, shall always be protected by you, O Goddess Mahālakṣmī, out of your affection for your son— even from thieves, fire, weapons, water, and even on the peak of a mountain, O beloved one; and he shall be capable of subduing thieves with his mere footstep.

O Goddess, even those who have committed the great sins of killing a Brahmin or a cow, once they have called to mind your face— which resembles the full moon and whose cheeks are rubbed by the shimmering divine rubies of your excellent earrings— release their bonds.

O Goddess Mahākālī, whose splendor is like the fire of cosmic destruction, even those whose hands and toes are bound by firm serpent-nooses as fetters are released from those terrible, great diseases through the recitation of Your name and the remembrance of Your two lotus feet.

O Bhairavī, Mother of all heroes, whose crown is adorned with a garland of Skanda, Brahmā, Indra, the Moon, and the Sun, and which is tawny like the filaments of a beautiful lotus— Bhairava has come to you for refuge;
forgive my transgression, forgive my transgression, O Śivā!
Thus praised by the great-souled Bhairava, the Great Goddess,
the Supreme Sovereign, then emerged, having burst forth from the linga.
Thus ends the Mālinī-daṇḍaka hymn.

Kiṇi vicce koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ. [Perform] the veiling of the face with the vajra-mudrā.
Aiṁ hūṁ phaṭ, svāhā to the vajra-fence! [This is] the touching of the ten doors.
Aiṃ cala akule kula acala hrīṃ hrūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
Kiṇi virce koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ pādukām.
The purification of the hands.
Aiṁ, salutation to the Blessed One, the Lotus of the Heart; Hrāṁ, the sandals for the two thumbs, O Śrī; Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā, the Lamp of the Kula; Hrīṁ, the sandals for the two index fingers, O Śrī.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, to Varvaraśikhā Hrūṃ, [I offer] sandals to the two venerable middle fingers.
Ghora, Aghora, Aghoramukhi, Vahurupa; Hre, [I worship] the sandals for the two ring fingers (anāmikā).
Chāṃ chī mahantārikāyai hrauṃ, [I offer] the sandals to the two little fingers (śrīkaniṣṭhābhyām).
Kiṇi vicce koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ, [I offer] the sandals to the two backs of the Śrīkara-tarās.
The ritual placement upon the limbs (karanyāsa).
Homage to the Blessed Lady Hṛtkamalā, the illustrious Ūrddhavaktrā; [I offer] the sandals.
Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula, whose face is preceded by Śrī; [I offer] the sandal-paste.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, O you with the curly locks, the sandals to the venerable southern face.
To the one who is Ghorā, Aghorā, Aghormukhī, and Bahurūpā; to the venerable Uttaravaktrā, [I offer] the sandal.
Chāṃ Chīṃ, to the Great Āryā, the Glorious One of the Western Face, [I offer] the sandals.
Kiṇi Vicce, to Koṅkaṇā, the venerable Parāparavaktrā, [I offer] the sandal.
The placement [of mantras] upon the face is the nyāsa.
Aiṃ! Salutation to the Blessed One, to the Lotus of the Heart; Hrāṃ! Salutation to the Heart.
Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula, Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head!
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, O you with the curly locks! Hūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Ghora, Aghora, Aghorāmukhī, Vahurūpā; Hreṃ, for the armor, Hūṃ.
Chāṃ chīṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes of Mahantārikā! Hrauṃ!
Kiṇi vicce koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ. Thus is the ritual placement on the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
The worship of the water vessel.
The sandals for the seat of the water-vessel: Aiṃ Haṃ, to the Lord of Heroes, Ānandaśaktibhairava-Ānanda, Saṃ, to the venerable Lord of the Water-Vessel (Śrījalapātra-bhaṭṭāraka), the sandals.
The six-limbed [practice].
Hrāṃ, the pādukā for the heart; hrīṃ, svāhā for the head.
Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Hraiṃ, hūṃ to the armor (kavaca). Hrauṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes (netratraya).
HRAḤ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ. Homage to the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood paste, the unbroken rice grains, and the flowers.
One should display the dhenumudrā.
The Gāyatrī.
The Consecration: Aiṃ! We know Kubjikā; we meditate upon her who is the lamp of the Kula; may that Kubjikā inspire us.
The worship of the argha vessel.

The sandals for the seat of the *argha* vessel: Aiṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hraḥ! Flash forth! O you of most terrible form, move, dance, strike, roar, vomit, subdue, slay, shatter, destroy the obstacles! Hūṃ Phaṭ Krauṃ!
Sandals for the venerable Mahākaumārikā Vicce! Pādukāṃ!
Aiṁ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī Phaṁ; the sandals for the venerable Śrī Arghapātrabhaṭṭārikā.
The six-limbed [practice].
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart; Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
HŪṂ, VAUṢAṬ to the crest-lock; HRAIṂ, HŪṂ to the armor; HRAUṂ, VAṢAṬ to the three eyes.
HRAḤ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ. Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers: NAMAH.
One should display the *yonimudrā*.
Purification of the Elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). Having formed the tortoise gesture (*kacchapa-mudrā*): aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ hsauṃ hsauṃ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ.
Self-worship.
Aiṁ, sandalwood, the sandals. Hrīṁ, unbroken rice grains, the sandals. Śrīṁ, the ashes of the hero, the sandals.

Hsphreṃ, the sandals of the one who deludes all people. Hsauṃ, the sandals of various umbrellas, ornaments, and flowers. Aiṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ, the flower and sandals for the self (ātman), [offered] to Ānandaśaktibhairava-ānanda, the Lord of Heroes, [with the mantra] śkṣmlvryīṃ. Aiṃ kusau, the sandals.
Thus concludes the self-worship.
The invocation.

Within the mandala of the venerable Samvarta, the power of bliss is established through the sequential steps; there is the most formidable [deity], the fourfold emission, that which resides in both Akula and Kula, another fivefold group, another sixfold group, four others,
and again another fivefold group of four— this is the mandala according to its true nature.
Bow down to that excellent Guru, the venerable Kujeśa Bhairava, by whom [all things] are interpenetrated.
I shall invoke; I invoke: the sandals of the primordial deity Śrī Ādideva, whose mandala is infinite.
O Trideva! Sandals for the human skin; sandals for the peacock skin.
Pādukā for Mūṣāsana. Aiṃ Thrau! Pādukā for the goddess Dambhaktī of Prastaradvīpa and for the Kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāka. Bali.
Aiṁ Śrīṁ Hrīṁ, the sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. Oblation.
Aiṃ Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ! To the venerable Lord of the Kula-gaṇas, the sandals! Oblation!
Invocation, seating, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers: salutation.
One should display the Tarjanī-daṇḍa-gaja mudrā.
The sandals for Padmāsana; the sandals for one's own Guru, Tuṣṇīśānandanātha Deva.
The sandals of the supreme guru Śrī Caryānandanātha.
The sandals of the supreme preceptor, the venerable Śrī Mitrānandadeva.
Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes (Vīrādhipati), śkṣmlvryīṃ!
To the venerable Śrītriśuddhibhaṭṭāraka, [I offer] the sandals. The sacrificial offering (bali).
[Recite] "Oṃ, salutations to the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood, the unbroken rice, and the flowers. One should display the *dhenu-mudrā* and the *yoni-mudrā*.
Aṃ astrāya phaṭ. Purification of the hands.
The ritual assignment of mantras to the hands and limbs (karāṅganyāsa).
HSAṂ, homage to the heart. KṢMAṂ, svāhā to the head. LVAṂ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
HŪṂ for the armor; VAṢAṬ for the three eyes; PHAṬ for the weapon.
Thus is the ritual placement on the hands and limbs (karāṅganyāsa).
Haṃ, the sandal at the place of the crest-lock; Saṃ, the sandal at the place of the head.
KṢAṂ, the pādukā on the forehead; MAṂ, the pādukā on the circle of the face.
Laṃ, the *pādukā* for the heart; vaṃ, the *pādukā* for the navel.
Raṃ, the sandal at the secret place; Yaṃ, the sandal on the knees; Ūṃ, the sandal on both feet.
Aṃ, the sandals for the Self of All.
Thus ends the Nyāsa of the Ninefold Self.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, [I offer] the sandals to the venerable Lord Navātman Nyāsa; [this is] the bali offering.
The sandals for the lotus-seat; the sandals for the corpse-seat.
Now, meditation.
Seated upon a lotus throne, reclining on a corpse, possessing ten faces and three eyes,
he is sky-colored, greatly radiant, and endowed with all the auspicious marks.
The eastern face is gold-colored, the southern is adorned with black,
the northern shall be yellow, and the one above that is tinted red.
To the right of the red [quarter] is the smoky-colored one, and to its north is the white;
above that is the yellow-colored one, and to the right of the yellow is the black.
They say the upper part is red, while that above it is white and most excellent;
the god has eighteen arms and is adorned with a necklace of severed heads.
The god holds a sword and a shield, as well as a trident and a goad,
a sacred thread, an excellent water-pot, a hand-drum, and a skull-topped staff.
He is well-equipped with arrows and a bow, beautifully adorned with a battle-axe and a bell;
he holds a discus and a mace in his hands, while his other two hands grant boons and fearlessness.
The Lord of Devas, beginning with the letter *ka* and bearing the *bindu*, is adorned with various ornaments;
he sits comfortably upon a corpse-seat which has the color of a corpse.
Thus, those men whose minds are disciplined who meditate upon this mandala consisting of nine aspects, which is the mandala of the Guru, shall quickly attain accomplishment.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Hskṣmlvryūṁ, to Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, the sovereign of heroes, śkṣmlvryīṁ, to the venerable Lord of the Navāgura Maṇḍala, [I offer] the sandals.
ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ; [I offer] the sandals to the venerable Navātma-gurumaṇḍala-bhaṭṭārikā.
The communal worship of the Gaṇas.
Mlūṃ P Mahāpūjā, the sandals for Gurumaṇḍalakubjikā.
Mlūṃ, E, O Great Worship! To the Śrī Śakti of the Guru-maṇḍala, [I offer] the pādukā.
Pluṃ, the sandals of the Śrī Devī of the maṇḍala of the supreme preceptor.
Slūṃ, the sandals of the supreme guru-maṇḍala, the venerable Jñānā.
Glūṃ, the sandals for Ājñānāyī at the circle of the eyebrows.
Salutation to the sandals of the lineage of gurus, both supreme and non-supreme, belonging to the essence of Śiva.
The sandals of the Śrīvidyā-tattva-gurumaṇḍala, who are both supreme and non-supreme.
The sandals of the Śrī Ātmatattva-gurumaṇḍala Aparājitā.
The sandals of Śrī Ājñākusumā; the sandals of Śrī Jayā.
The sandals for Śrī Vijayā. The sandals for Śrī Ajitā.
The sandals for Śrī Aparājitā; the sandals for Śrī Haṃ Śāntyatītā.
The pādukā of Śrī Yaṃ for peace; the pādukā of Śrī Raṃ for knowledge.
Śrī Vaṃ, the sandals for the sake of sustenance; Śrī Laṃ, the sandals for the sake of cessation.
The sandals to Śrī Kulabhairava; the sandals to Śrī Kulanāthabhairava.
To the venerable Kulatumburubhairava, [I offer] the sandals.
To the venerable Kulakapāṭabhairava, [I offer] the sandals.
The sandals to Śrīkula-Ājñā-Bhairava; the sandals to Śrīkula-Ājñā-Devī.
KṢĀṂ KṢĪṂ KṢŪṂ KṢAḤ, the sandals for the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla).
Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaḥ glauṃ, the sandals to Śrī Kulagaṇeśvara.
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, the sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha.
Kroṃ! O Śrī Mahākaumārikā Vicce, [I invoke] the sandals!

Aiṁ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ! Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Mahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ!
To the Navātman, the venerable Guru-maṇḍala, [I offer] the sandals.
The six-limbed [practice].
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṃ, for the armor, hūṃ. Hrauṃ, for the three eyes, ṣaṭ.

Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hreṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hrauṃ,
O you whose form is Rudra, Hraḥ, [I worship] the sandals. Aiṃ Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ Trailokyākarṣaṇī Hrīṃ Kāmāṅgadrāvaṇī Klīṃ Strīṃ Mahākṣobhakāriṇī Aiṃ Sauṃ Saḥ, [I worship] the sandals of Śrī.

Salutation to the Blessed One, Hsphreṁ Kubjikā! Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ! O Terrible One, O Non-terrible One, O You Whose Face is Non-terrible! Chāṁ Chīṁ Kiṇi Vicce! Salutation to the sandals! Salutation to the sandals of the entire seat of mantras, the lion-throne, the primary seat, the secondary seat, the minor seat, the field, the minor field, the confluence, the minor confluence, the divine accomplishment, and the wheel of the covenant!
Whatever has been said or not said, all of that—aiṃ śrī—to the Heart, the sandal-paste.
Thus is the offering for each individual.
[Perform] the invocation, the installation, and [offer] sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, and flowers; [say] "Namaḥ. One should display the Yoni-mudrā.
The Three Bindus. Homage to Śrīnātha. Homage to Śrīsiddhinātha.
Homage to the venerable Kujeśanātha; salutations again and again. Thus ends the worship of the maṇḍala of the gurus.
Pādukā for Padmāsana. HSKMLVRYŪṂ, pādukā for the venerable lineage of Gurus. Bali offering.
To the sandals of Padmāsanā: Aiṃ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ, the sandals and offering to the venerable Oṣadhikarmabhaṭṭārikā.
The sandals for the bull-throne; the sandals for the lion-throne.
Aiṁ HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, to the Lord of Heroes (Vīrādhipati) accompanied by the power of Śrīkaṇṭhanātha, [I offer] the sandals (pādukā). The sacrificial offering (bali).
Brahmāṇyādi || Sandal for the one seated upon a swan; sandal for the one seated upon a bull.
The sandal for the peacock-throne; the sandal for the eagle-throne.
The sandals for the one seated upon a buffalo; the sandals for the one seated upon an elephant.
The sandals for the seat of the pretas; the sandals for the human corpse-chain.
O Aghorā, O Amoghā, O Varadā, O Vimalā, O Brahmanī, O Vicce, [I worship] the sandals.
Aghore, Amoghe, Valade, Vimale, Māheśvarī, Vicce—[I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ Aghore Amoghe Varade Vimale Krauṃ Māri Vicce Pādukāṃ.
Oghore, Amoghe, Varade, Vimalē, Vaiṣṇavi, Vicce, [I worship] the sandals.
Oghore, Amoghe, Varade, Vimale, Vārāhi, Vicce, [bestow] the sandals!
O Āghorī, O Amoghā, O Varadā, O Vimalā, O Indrāgnī, O Vicce, [I worship] the sandals.
Oghore, Amoghe, Varade, Vīmale, Cāmuṇḍā, Vicce, [I worship] the sandals.
O Aghorā, O Amoghā, O Amoghā, O Bestower of Boons, O Immaculate One, O Mahālakṣmī, O Vicce—[I worship] the sandals.
This is their offering.
The pādukā for Ādhāraśakti; the pādukā for Anantāsana.
A sandal for one who subsists on bulbs.
Sandals for the one whose seat is the nara-tree; sandals for the one whose seat is the leaf.
The sandals for the one seated upon the filaments; the sandals for the one seated upon the pericarp.
The sandals for the lotus throne. The sandals for the lion throne.
The sandal for the one seated upon a buffalo; the sandal for the one seated upon Śumbha.
The sandals for the seat of Niśumbha. *Namaḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to Caṇḍacogrā, *namaḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ* the sandals. The sandals of Śrī Rudracaṇḍā. The sandals of Śrī Pracaṇḍā.
The sandals of Śrī Caṇḍogrā; the sandals of Śrī Caṇḍanāyikā.
The sandals of Śrīcaṇḍā; the sandals of Śrīcaṇḍavatī.
The sandals of Śrī Caṇḍarūpā; the sandals of Śrī Aticaṇḍikā.
Hsphreṁ! The sandals of Śrī Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī. Oṃ hrīṁ! O Rājapradā, Hsphreṁ!
O Ugracaṇḍā, O Crusher of Enemies, Hūṃ Phreṁ! Always protect you and me, Juṃ Saḥ! O Mṛtyuharā, homage to the sandals!
This is the bali offering for them.
The sandals for the one in the lotus posture: Aiṁ Rīṅgaṇḍi Piṅgaṭī Kuḍu Kaṇḍāyai Svāhā! Vāgeśvarī, the Great Mahantārikā, Vicce! Pā (*). The offering (bali).
The pādukā to Ādhāraśakti; the pādukā to Anantāsana.
The sandals for one who subsists on bulbs; the sandals for one who subsists on meat.
A sandal for the Lotus Seat; a sandal for the Sun Seat.
The sandals for the one seated upon the pericarp; the sandals for the one seated upon the lotus.
Pādukā for the seat of the five pretas: Hsauṃ Svāhā! Pādukā for the seat of the fire-pretas: Hsauṃ Svāhā!
The sandals for the bull-throne; the sandals for the lion-throne.
Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hreṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hrauṃ,
Rudrarūpe Hraḥ, [worship] the sandals (pādukā). Aiṃ Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ Trailokyākarṣaṇī Hrīṃ Kāmaṅgadrāvaṇī Klīṃ Strīṃ Mahākṣobhakāriṇī Aiṃ Sauṃ.
He [worships] the Śrīpādukā: *Namo bhagavati hsphreṃ kubjikāyai hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ ghore aghore aghorāmukhi cchāṃ cchīṃ kiṇi vicce pādukāṃ*.
Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṁ Kubjikā! Śrāṁ Śrīṁ Śrūṁ! Ṅa Ña Ṇa! O you whose face is not terrible (Aghorāmukhī)! Chāṁ Chīṁ Kiṇi Vicce! [I worship] the sandals.
To the Blessed One: Siddhe Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ Kubjike Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrūṃ Khage E Ghore Aghore Amorāmukhī Kiṇi Vicce Pādukāṃ. Thus, the offering (bali) is made for each [deity] individually.

Whosoever among the Yoginīs are born of the *pīṭhas*, born of the *kṣetras*, born together, born of yoga, born from the womb, born of the *kula*, or born of the *saṃdoha*; whosoever among the Yoginīs are sky-travelers (*khecarī*), earth-travelers (*bhūcarī*), range-travelers (*gocarī*), single-syllabled, two-syllabled, three-syllabled, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine-syllabled, who traverse the three worlds—
Accept the offering of those who have appeared as they are; grant me success! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Three handfuls of water [are offered]. || ||
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, the sovereign of heroes, Śkṣmlvryī, the venerable lord of the twenty-eight rites, [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṁ ŚKṢMLVRYĪ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ; the sandals for the venerable mistress of the twenty-eight rites.
Bali.
Ṣaḍaṃśa: Hrāṃ, obeisance to the heart; Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock; Hraiṃ, hūṃ to the armor.

The sandals of the entire seat of mantras, the lion-throne, the pedestal, the secondary pedestal, the field, the secondary field, the gathering place, the divine accomplishment, and the wheel of the pledge.
Whatever has been said or not said, all that—to the Śrī Hṛdaya, the pādukā.
The offering (bali) is made with the root mantra. Invocation, water for the feet, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers: *namaḥ*.
One should display the Dhenuyonimudrā. Thus concludes the ritual worship (karmapūjā).
The sandals for the lotus posture.

[Perform] the invocation and so forth; one should display the *trikhaṇḍā* mudrā.
The pādukā to Ādhāraśakti; the pādukā to Anantāsana.
A sandal for Kaṇṇāsana; a sandal for Nārāsana.
The sandals for the lotus seat; the sandals for the filament seat.
The sandal for the one seated on the pericarp; the sandal for the one in the lotus posture.
The sandals for the seat of the five pretas. The sandals for the lord of the moon-maṇḍala, the seat of the Brahma-pretas. The sandals for the lord of the sun-maṇḍala, the seat of the Viṣṇu-pretas.
To the sovereign of the fire-maṇḍala, seated upon the corpse of Rudra, [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṃ, the sandals for the lord of the Brahma-maṇḍala, the Īśvara-preta.
To the Lord of the Śakti-maṇḍala, together with the corpse of Sanāśiva, [I offer] the sandals.
The sandals for the bull-throne; the sandals for the lion-throne.
Meditative absorption.
One should visualize the God seated upon a bull, having the color of the sky, established in form,
with one face, three eyes, and bearing eighteen arms.
In her right hands, she holds a *ḍamaru* drum, an arrow, a sword, a small vajra, a conch, and the playing of a lute, as well as the gestures of granting boons (*varada*) and fearlessness (*abhaya*).
In the left [hands], he holds a khaṭvāṅga, a trident, a bow, a shield, and a noose;
a bell, a skull-cup, and a lute, as well as the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*) which destroys all suffering.
Bound with a silken cloth, the goddess Jāvāmorusthā has one face,
three eyes, and is described as being of a reddish dawn-like color.
Two-armed, granting boons with her right hand and dispelling fear with her left, she stands upon a lion;
she is richly adorned with various ornaments and possesses all auspicious marks.
This one, whose nature is the bliss of Bhairava, is proclaimed as the eldest among the eldest;
by meditating thus upon Mahādeva, human beings quickly attain perfection.
Thus ends the fifth meditation. Homage!

Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hreṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hsauṃ, O you whose form is Rudra, Hraḥ, [I worship] the sandals. Aiṃ E Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ Trailokyākarṣaṇī Hrīṃ Kāmāṅgadrāvaṇī Klīṃ Strīṃ Mahākṣobhakāriṇī Aiṃ Soṃ Saḥ, [I worship] the sandals of Śrī.

The garland mantra with three *añjali* gestures: *Oṃ namaḥ sarvasiddhiyoginībhyaḥ | namaḥ sarvasiddhimātṛbhyaḥ | namo nityoditānandananditāyai sakalakulacakranāyikāyai bhagavatyai caṇḍakāpālinyai | tadyathā:*

Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ || Khphreṃ! O Supreme Swan, bestower of the path to Nirvāṇa, pacifier of calamities and misfortunes, destroyer of all evils, enemies, and afflictions, ferry across the ocean of all disasters, crusher of all foes, O Goddess, come, come! Laugh, laugh! Valla, valla! [O you who end with human blood!]
O consumer of fat, crush, crush my enemies! Eat, eat! Pierce, pierce with the trident!
Cut, cut with the sword! Strike them until you have accomplished all my desires!
O supremely compassionate Blessed One, wearer of the form of Mahābhairava!

In the year measured by thirty-three, the year in which all mantra-suns bow down, O Goddess Mahākālī, destroyer of Time! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Be gracious! Hrīṃ! Make the daughters of gods and asuras afflicted with passion! Hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
After these, the offering (bali) should be made. [Perform] the invocation (āvāhana) and so forth. One should display the yoni-mudrā.

In the ten directions: Lūṃ, the sandals for Indra; the offering. Ruṃ, the sandals for Agni.

At the four gates: Khpreṃ, the sandals of Kramagaṇapatinātha; Khphreṃ, the sandals of Kramagaṇapatināthavallabhāmbā.
KH PHREṂ! O Lord Kṣetrapāla, fierce with the power to destroy all things, [I worship] your sandals!
Khphreṃ! O Mother, beloved of the Kṣetrapāla Mahāsakalasaṃhāravalotkaṭa, [I worship] your sandals.
KH PHREṂ! To Kramavaṭukanātha, the sandals!
Khphreṃ, the sandals of Kramavaṭukanātha and his beloved consort Ambā.
Khphreṃ! The sandals of the Lord of Oḍiyāna-pīṭha!
Khphreṃ! The sandals of Vṛṣasaṃkaṭanātha.
KH PHREṂ! The sandals of Sarvasaṃketanātha.
Khphreṃ! O Mother Sarvasaṃhāriṇī, [bestow] the sandals!
KH PHREṂ! O Great Lord of the Kanavīra cremation ground, [grant] the sandals!
Khpreṃ Heṃ Heṃ, [I offer] the *pādukā* to the Yoginīs. This is the *bali* offering for them.
In the square line is the lineage of gurus: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Vīranātha.
Bali: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of the Lord of the Ten-Necked One (Rāvaṇa).
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Krodhamuninātha; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Vasiṣṭhanātha.

Khphreṃ! O Goddess Kiṃkiṇī Ambā, [bestow] the sandals!

On the inner circle: Aiṃ Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ. On the outer circle: Aiṃ Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ.

In the three [sections] of the Vajrī: Aiṁ! Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṁ! To Kubjikā, Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ! O Terrible One, Non-terrible One, She Whose Face is Non-terrible! Chāṁ Chīṁ Kiṇi Vicce! [Salutation to] the sandals! The offering (bali).
Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṁ Kubjikā! Śrāṁ Śrīṁ Śrūṁ! Obeisance to the one whose face is not terrible (Aghorāmukhī)!
Chāṁ Chīṁ Kiṇi Vicce! [I offer] the sandals! [I offer] the sacrificial oblation (bali)!
To the Blessed One, Siddhe hsphrāṃ hsphrīṃ hsphrūṃ Kubjike śrāṃ śrīṃ śrūṃ Khaṇe aiṃ Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhī Kiṇi Vicce, [I offer] the sandals. The oblation.
[Having performed] the triple añjali [with the root mantra], the bali offering, and the worship with the six limbs of the root mantra.
The Gāyatrī.
Khphreṃ: let us know the Goddess Siddhilakṣmī; let us meditate upon her who is superior by nine; may that Lakṣmī inspire us.
Having performed the invocation and other rites, one should display the yoni-mudrā.
The worship of Kālī. The ritual ground for worship. The sacrificial offering on the ritual ground, beginning with the recitation of the mantra.
Having sipped water with the threefold truth: *Phreṃ*, svāhā to the principle of the self (*ātmatattva*); *Phreṃ*, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (*vidyātattva*).
Phreṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva.
The ritual placement (nyāsa): Svāhā! To the weapon (astra), Phaṭ!
The purification of the hands.
Oṃ phreṃ, homage to the two little fingers. Siddhikarālī, homage to the two ring fingers.
Hrīṁ chrīṁ hūṁ, salutation to the two middle fingers. Strīṁ phreṁ, salutation to the two index fingers.
*Namaḥ* to the two thumbs; *namaḥ* [to the heart]. *Svāhā* to the weapon (*astra*); *namaḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands.
This is the *kara-nyāsa*.
Oṃ phreṃ, homage to the heart! Siddhikarālī, svāhā to the head! Hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock! Strīṃ phreṃ, hūṃ to the armor!
*Namaḥ* to the three eyes, *vaṭ*. *Svāhā* to the weapon, *phaṭ*. Thus is the ritual placement of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*).
The worship of the argha vessel.
For the offering of the seat, the sandals: Oṃ phreṃ siddhikarālī hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ svāhā.
The six limbs: Oṃ phreṃ, homage to the heart.
Siddhikarāli, svāhā to the head! Hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ, voṣaṭ to the crest-lock!
Strīṃ phreṃ, hūṃ to the armor; namaḥ vaṣaṭ to the three eyes; svāhā phaṭ to the weapon.

Oṃ phreṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ, homage to Siddhikarālīśvara! Having invoked [the deity] with the Ākarṣaṇī mudrā, perform the veiling (avaguṇṭhana). [Perform] the invocation (āvāhana) and installation (sthāpana); [offer] sandalwood, unbroken rice, and flowers—homage!
One should display the Dhenuyoni-mudrā.
The Gāyatrī.
Oṃ Phreṃ! We know the Great Mantra; we meditate upon Kālasaṃkarṣaṇī; may that Śakti inspire us.
Self-worship.
Oṃ phreṃ, sandalwood, the sandals! Oṃ phreṃ, unbroken rice, the sandals!
Oṃ Phreṃ, [I worship] the vermilion and the sandals.
Oṃ phreṃ, the sandals of Mohanī. Oṃ phreṃ, the sandals of the flower.
The three drops: Khphreṃ Oṃ Phreṃ, homage to the one consisting of the full moon!
The seat.
Oṃ phreṃ, homage to the seat of the seven skulls. Oṃ phreṃ phreṃ phreṃ, homage to the seat of Mahāśivā. [This is] the meditation.
One should meditate upon the goddess Kālī, who is exceedingly secret, ten-faced, and three-eyed;
she is black in color, possesses great splendor, has eight arms and a slender waist,
and is a deity with faces of various colors, whose nature is the essence of the sun.
Clad in a tiger skin and adorned with ornaments of bone.
In his right hands, he holds a trident, a goad, a vajra, and a mallet;
likewise, in his left, he holds a khaṭvāṅga staff, a noose, a vessel, and the head of a corpse.
Wandering through the king of sequences, which resembles a thousand suns,
she proceeds toward the single accomplishment for the sake of the central meaning of the eight extremes.
Cit-kālī, situated in the midst of the Kula, is like a form of light within the Lord;
she is supreme liberation, the Vidyā who transcends all states of being, and is beyond the reach of the mind.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Threefold salutation with joined palms.

Salutation to the three eyes, vaṣaṭ! Svāhā to the weapon, phaṭ! One should display the yoni-mudrā.

The sandals for the seat of the *argha* vessel: *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ pādukām*. The sandals: *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ pādukām*.
The six-limbed [practice].
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, salutation to the heart. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, svāhā to the head.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, Vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, Hūṃ to the armor (kavaca).
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, Vaṣaṭ to the three eyes. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, Phaṭ to the weapon.
[Recite] "Oṃ, salutations! [This is for] the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood paste, the unbroken rice grains, and the flowers. One should display the *yonimudrā*.
Self-worship.
Aiṃ, sandalwood, the sandals. Klīṃ, unbroken rice, the sandals. Sauṃ, vermilion, the sandals.
Aiṃ, the sandals of Mohanī. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, the sandals of the Self-flower. The three points (bindus).
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, [I worship] the Sandals.
The worship of the Goddess’s seat.
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ, the sandals for the one seated upon a red lotus.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ; the sandals for the seat of the five pretas.
Meditative absorption.
I worship her who has the luster of the orb of the rising sun, who possesses four arms and three eyes,
and who holds a noose, a goad, arrows, and a bow.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
The triple añjali gesture.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ Kilhrīṃ Hskhlhrīṃ Sklhrīṃ, [I worship] the sandals of the Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī.
The sacrificial offering.
The Gāyatrī.
Aiṃ, we know Tripurā; Klīṃ, may we meditate upon Kāmeśvarī; Tanna Sauṃ, may she impel us. [This is] the offering (bali).
With the root mantra, perform three *añjali* gestures; perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*); perform the invocation and other rites; and display the *yonimudrā*.
Now, the mantra for the removal of wrinkles:
On the western side of the stone slab at Thaṇḍilīyaṅthujavalāsa.
Having offered two handfuls of water for the sake of the deceased.
Aiṃ! All the pīṭhas and upapīṭhas, as well as the doors and side-doors, the kṣetras, upakṣetras, and sandohas, situated in every direction.
The yoginīs and the lords of the heroes of yoga have all arrived there;
this is the festival of the Great Wheel, where Śrīnātha, the bestower of boons, is present for me.
O Goddess, for those devotees who are intent upon the teaching and devoted to the worship of the Guru’s feet,
may I always be the bestower of all accomplishments.
O Goddess, O Meru-melaka, you who delight in the heroes and yoginīs, accept this offering (bali) here according to the practice of the samaya.
May those throngs of Yoginīs, who are filled with hosts of [other] Yoginīs, cut away the hearing, memory, mind, nourishment, flesh, fat, bones, and life of the wicked.
May those throngs of Yoginīs, crowded with hosts of [deities], cut away evil dreams such as kuhukā and the like, ill-omened portents, and wicked words of the malevolent.
The three essential seats (pīṭhas) proclaimed among those beginning with Oṃkāra,
as well as the medicinal herbs, the gathering places (saṃdohas), and [the seats] in the cardinal and intermediate directions,
exist within the cosmic egg of the protector of the earth and in all other locations.
May the yoginīs, whose souls are united with yoga, remain steadfast in their commitments;
may the heroic lords of heroes, the deities, abide in truth.
The Siddhas, the Putrakas, the Ācāryas, and the Sādhakas sleep upon the earth,
whether in a city or a village, in a forest or by an excellent river.
In ponds, wells, solitary trees, cremation grounds, or in the circles of the Mothers (mātṛmaṇḍala),
may all those various beings born of the *vaṭa* tree, assuming manifold forms,
be entirely satisfied and accept the sacrificial offering (*bali*) from every side.
Even though I have come to them for refuge, they shall grant me all this fruit:
whatever karma has been accumulated by me, whatever I shall do, and whatever I have done.
May those who contemplate me be satisfied by the offering of leaves and flowers;
may all my actions be successful, and may all my faults be pacified.
I bow to the venerable Kū-kārā, who bestows the power of Śiva.
Thus ends the *samayabali*.
Three handfuls of joined palms.
The sandals for the bull-throne; the sandals for the lion-throne.
Aiṃ Haṃ! To the bliss of Ānandaśakti-Bhairava, the sovereign lord of heroes, ŚKṢMLVRYŪ-ĪṂ; to the venerable Paścimamūlasthāna-Bhaṭṭārikā, [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṃ ŚKṢMLVRYŪṂ ĪṂ! O Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, O Sovereign Queen of the Great Vidyās, HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ! [I offer] the sandals to the venerable Bhaṭṭārikā of the Western Root Abode. [The six limbs.]
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrāṃ, svāhā to the head. Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṃ, *hūṃ* for the armor; Hrauṃ, *vaṣaṭ* for the three eyes; Hraḥ, *phaṭ* for the weapon. Oblation.
Invocation and so forth; the Yoni-mudrā; the Nirvāṇa-chāyā.
The great lineage of Tvaika.
KṢĀṂ KṢĪṂ KṢŪṂ! O Guardian of the Field, accept this offering; svāhā!
Aiṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ! O Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha, accept this bali offering; svāhā!
Aiṁ gāṁ gīṁ gūṁ gaḥ glauṁ! O Śrī Kulagaṇeśvara, accept this offering; svāhā!
Aiṃ Hūṃ!
O Great Kanavīra, Lord of the cremation ground, accept this bali offering, svāhā!
Aiṁ Śkhphrīṁ, O Siddhicāṇḍeśvarī, accept this offering; svāhā!
Aiṃ! O you who move through the sky, from all the classes of beings, accept this offering; svāhā!
Aiṃ! To all beings, accept this offering; svāhā!
[Recite] "Oṃ, salutations! [This is for] the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood paste, the unbroken rice grains, and the flowers. One should then display the *yonimudrā*.
The libation.
Homage to the illustrious Nātha! Homage to the illustrious Siddhinātha! Homage again and again to the illustrious Jeśanātha!
Thus ends the western section.
This is the offering for Thaṇḍilijavalāli Thupāṭajayatumbureśvarī.

I offer this oblation. Oṃ khphreṃ! To the yoginīs who move through the sky, to the yoginīs who move through the earth, to the yoginīs who move through the directions, and to the yoginīs who move through the great void—this oblation, consisting of meat, rice, *ali*, *caru*, lamps, and betel, [is offered] hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā!
Oṃ glauṃ glauṃ! O Gaṇapati, grant me the prosperity of dharma, artha, and kāma, as well as success; O Gaṇa, accept this worship and offering, protect me, and bring about peace—svāhā!

Oṃ, homage to those who cause obstacles! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kṣyoṃ Kṣyeṃ! To the Kṣetrapāla with tawny matted hair, accept the incense, lamp, flowers, liquor, and meat; in the form of Bhairava, forgive me and grant me boons, svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ! O Goddess, to the son Vaṭuka, with matted hair like a *kali* flower and tawny eyes, accept this offering for you.

May she— who utters "Carma-muṇḍā Vauṃ Chīṃ Phreṃ," who devours, drinks, and dances with loud laughter of "ha ha ha ha"— dispel all fear for the meditator in the midst of wicked thieves, enemies, and pestilence, during planetary afflictions, in the abode of the Gaṇas, amidst a thunderbolt strike, in battle, at the king’s gate, or in a flood of water.
The Mother of Mantras, *kili kilita kali*, who utters the speech of the Kaula tradition.

The syllables *sā-śu-ṣ-kā*, which take any form at will, along with *ya-la-ra-va-pa-ṭa-hā*, the sounds *hā-hā-hūṃ*, and the *ucchiṣṭa-nīlakaṇṭha*— these are praised as the friends of the immortals when placed upon the head of the *bindu*.

Making the sound *phreṃ phreṃ phreṃ*, she is drenched in blood; being struck with a sword, she is full of wrath; licking the tip of her tongue, she makes the sound *la la la la la*; causing the creeper to run, she drinks.

Kṛṣṇā, the messenger known as Kāmā, praised for her divine qualities, merged within the Bindu and Nāda; she bestows accomplishment, has reached the supreme state, and, having increased the limbs of the ritual arena, is worshipped.
Bold, joined with the guardians of the world, the sin, and the wind, followed by the king, with the sixth [vowel] and the bindu, devoted to the lineage-observance, she is the savior known as Kuṇḍalā.

May that Bhīṣaṇī Bhadrakālī, who is proclaimed as the power of Rudra, grant auspiciousness; she whose form is *kāṃ kīṃ kūṃ kama*, who has entered the lineage of the Akula, and who devours those who harbor hatred.

May she who is known as Sāmeśrī-Kubjikā bestow the supreme, divine, and unfailing Vāma; may Cāmuṇḍā, the Kaulinī of the Koṅkaṇa lineage, grant it within the tradition of the Kulakrama on the path of the Kaulas.

Proclaimed on the Left Path (vāmamārga), her abode made manifest as Mālinī with the body of the Bindu; she who consists of both Akula and Kula has entered the circle of yogis within the Maṇḍala of Oṃkāra.
That Goddess, the Mother of the World, whose form is formidable, is praised by the assembly of sages upon the lap of Śrīnātha.
The Mothers, headed by Śivāsaka, reside in the wheel of Śrīnātha.

Worshipped by Śrīkaṇṭha, known as Ambikā, she resides in the four yuga-endowed supreme liṅgas; established in the sacred seats (pīṭhas), she fulfills all desires, possessing the power of the sixty-four arts, shining forth from the Kaula path, and renowned by the name Śrī Kubjikā.

I bow with devotion to that Goddess who possesses the threefold path, who consists of three syllables, who is of three kinds, whose abode is manifest, and who is differentiated by the five [elements] from beginning to end.
May the Mother Kubjikā— the dark one, whose form is a skeleton, who utters most intense sounds, the terrifying one who devours—
grant the great knowledge of the divine, inexhaustible current.

In ancient times, while the ocean of milk was being churned by the gods and the asuras,

The goddess resembles lac-dye in color, possessing a radiance equal to a ruby;
she has eighteen arms and is adorned with ornaments of jewels.
The goddess, assuming a gentle form, has three eyes and nine faces;
she holds a sword, a trident, a vajra, a ḍiṇḍima drum, and likewise a mallet.
A mace, a lotus, an excellent vessel, and a pheṭakā are resplendent in the right hands;
while an elephant-goad, a bell, a skull-cup, a khaṭvāṅga, and a water-pot are in the left hands.
Holding a blue lotus and the syllable *Bhayaṃ* (the seed-syllable of fearlessness) in her left hand,

The Goddess, resembling a creeper of lightning, with a form as crooked as a serpent—
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśa, and Sadāśiva [are within her].

O Goddess, Mother of the three worlds, salutations to you who are the embodiment of Śakti;
you reside between the Iḍā and Piṅgalā nerves, having the form of a lotus fiber.

Gaurī, known as Umā, resides in the heart, possessing the splendor of twelve suns.
In the void, abiding within the void, she is the sustainer of life-breath known as Haṃsa.
The supreme goddess named Lambā moves from south to north;
having emerged at the tip of the nose, she flows along the central channel.

In the gross and the subtle, in one's own upward-rushing [state], in the two cavities of dharma and adharma,

The goddess Bhramaṇī, Bhrāmaṇī, Gaurī, who flows through the machinery of illusion;
she is Svacchandabhairavī, Krodhabhairavī, and Unmattabhairavī.

I bow to Kṣetrapāla, the lord of bhūtas, pretas, and the like, together with the host of planetary deities.
Clad in red garments, with a mass of flaming tawny matted locks, bearing a staff as fierce as a host of fevers,
he is fair as the golden peaks of Mount Meru at sunrise.
I bow to Vaṭukanātha, the son of Gaurī.
Hantā! O you who destroy this worldly suffering, who have stilled the fear of existence, whose body destroys all obstacles—gāṁ gīṁ gūṁ gaiḥ gaḥ!
O you who possess the six limbs, who have gone to the multitude of the sky, O Siddhi, bestower of all aims!
Oṃ glūṃ! O Mudrā, known as Gajā, who has moved upon the wind of Ga-sa, you who have many eyes like a rat and possess many tusks;
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ gāṃ! O Gaṇeśa, whose face is that of the lord of elephants, O Lord of Obstacles, homage be to you!
Belonging to Brahmā.
Victory to her who rides a swan, who resembles molten gold, who has four faces and three eyes,
and who holds in the tips of her hands the *brahmakūrca* vessel, a water-pot, a radiant staff,
and a lotus-seed rosary; she of beautiful attire, seated at the base of the petals of the directions beginning with the southeast (the direction of Indra).
I bow to her whose variegated body is adorned with perfumes and other ornaments, and who bears the weight of an excellent mass of matted locks.
Belonging to Maheśvarī.
One should meditate upon that Māheśī at the base of the son of the Fire-god (Agni), who is white like dense snow, holding a skull, a skull-topped staff, a drum, a gesture of fearlessness,
a trident, and a large sword; she is radiant with three eyes and possesses a crescent moon atop her matted locks which are tawny at their tips.
One should worship with perfumes and other offerings that [deity] who, having ascended the bull, constantly travels through the sky.
The Komaṛīya [tradition].

One should worship Kaumārī with perfumes and flowers—she who is rich in youth, possessing a most beautiful face, radiant like saffron, and exceedingly lovely; she who holds in her own right hands a spear, a noose, and a goad, as well as the gesture of fearlessness; she who is intoxicated by wine, expansive, and has a pair of sparkling eyes.
Adorned with all ornaments, she is dark-hued like a flame, with her face turned toward the direction of the root.
Belonging to Viṣṇu.
In the southwest direction, at the base of the leaf, one should meditate upon Vaiṣṇavī, who has limbs as dark as a water-laden cloud, beautiful hair, and who holds a bell,
a conch, a skull, and a discus in her staff-like arms;
she is seated upon Garuḍa and is illuminated by a crown made of jewels.
She who is perpetually delighted by the intoxication of honey should be worshipped with perfumes and other offerings until she is satisfied and restless.
To Vārāhī.

Vārāhī, boar-faced, holds a shield, a sword, a mace, and a plough; she is adorned with shimmering jeweled earrings that graze her cheeks at the base of her ears on the western side, and she stands upon a fierce,
mountain-peak-like boar worshipped by the entire universe.
One should worship her, whose teeth are most beautiful and whose body possesses a luster smoky with incense, with perfumes and other offerings.
The wife of Indra.

One should constantly worship the intoxicated Indrāṇī, who is praised by the best of gods, seated upon her own elephant, wearing a crown resembling the orb of the moon, and holding in her four lotus-hands a bow, a goad, a conch, a trident, and an arrow, with the wind as the base of the petals of her [lotus-like] face.
To Cāmuṇḍā.
And Cāmuṇḍā, with a fierce laugh, formidable and wide-baring fangs, a terrifying face, and three eyes, holding a sword, a trident, a skull-cup, and a shield in her own hands—
at the base of the petal of the eastern direction, she is fleshless, red-eyed, and brings fear to the three worlds.
One should worship Kālī, who is adorned with skeletons, whose hair stands upright, and who dwells in the cremation ground.
By Mahālakṣmī.
Afterwards, one should worship her who is of wondrous form, with a most beautiful face, possessing the luster of pure gold,

holding in her lotus-hands a rosary, the gesture of fearlessness, a shining lotus, and *mātuluṅga* fruits; she who is honored by the gods, the serpent-king Jalaṃdhara, and others, and who is endowed with a hundred thousand [perfections].
O Lord, [I salute] Lakṣmī, who is embraced at the base of the petals of the directions by Your lofty and full breasts.
All these [are] Brahmāṇī and the others.
Aśitāṅga and so forth.

Homage to Sitāṅga, Ruru, and the one known as Caṇḍa; to Krodheśa, Unmatta, Kapāla, and Bhairava; and in the midst of Palāśa, to the one named Bhīṣaṇa. I bow to these Bhairavas, beginning with Hetuka, who are designated as Saṃhāra.
He who is the causal one, the controller, and the ender of the city; he who is fire, the Vetāla, and the tongue of the sacrificial flame;
he who is Time and the Skull, as well as the One-footed; he who is indeed of terrifying form and fearsome appearance.
To Ugracaṇḍā.
O slayer of Mahiṣa, O you of great illusion, O destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa,
O goddess who takes away the blood-seed, I bow to Ugracaṇḍī.
To Vagalā.

The king, who is like a fire, becomes as cold as ice toward the disputant who acts like a mute deer; he who is prone to anger becomes equanimous; the wicked man becomes virtuous; the swift traveler becomes lame;
and the arrogant man becomes humble—everyone is rendered inert when constrained by the mechanism of your command.
O Śrī Nityā Vagalāmukhī, O auspicious one, salutations to you every day!
By means of the three powers.

Red, white, and black, possessing the threefold course of the river, the three goddesses are the three measures; having praised you, those who have attained the various states have achieved the three groups of success.
Whether young, child, or old, she becomes the one who transcends existence, the awakener of the three times.
May the daily worship, which is auspicious and a limb of Śiva, bestow victory upon the one who possesses a beautiful womb.
[This is] by Hanubhairava.
I bow to the Supreme Lord Rudra, who has the form of Bhairava,
the God characterized by the three worlds, the sovereign Lord of the Ḍāmaras.
By Nāṭeśvarī.
Squeezing the entire universe with both hands, he causes it to boil and overflow until it is thoroughly cooked; with his mouth wide open like a towering fruit,
he drinks again and again the essence of the three worlds as if intoxicated.
May Mahābhairava protect me through the ritual procedure consisting of the grand display of the dance of the sacrificial ground.
The fifth belongs to Vārāhī.
Salutations to you, O Great Māyā, who bear the name Vārāhī;
O fierce one with the face of a boar, who holds a vajra-tusk!
By Siddheśvarī.
O Maheśānī, she has one face and three eyes, is adorned with a crescent moon as her crest-jewel,
possesses four hands, and has two hands joined in the gesture of prayer (añjali).
Seated upon a ghost-throne, she is red in color and intensely radiant;
the goddess is like ten million suns, possessing a watery nature and great splendor.
Of Chinnamastā.
At the navel is a white lotus, above which is the stainless mandala of the fierce-rayed sun;
there, for the sake of the arising of the activity of Dharma— the sole essence of cyclic existence and the mother of the three worlds—
is the praised Chinnamastā, possessing a triple body within that center at the junction of the three paths.
I pay homage to her, whose form is wisdom, who removes the fear of death, the mudrā of the yoga of the Yoginī.

The letter *ū* is the dancing feet; *ha-sa-kṣa-ma-la-va-bu-jo* is the belly; *agni-liṅga* (the fire-linga) is the tail; *vāyu-vyāṅghri* (the wind-foot) is the skin; *añji* is the sky; *śaśi-sakala* (the full moon) is the head; it is joined with the *bindu*, *nāda*, and the half-moon;
it is the stream of the Gaṅgā from the Jina; it is straight, the supreme digit (*paramakalā*), Bhairava, whose form is the mantra.
May the ninefold Lord, the supreme teacher of all, the auspicious Bhairava Kujeśa, protect us.
Brahmāṇī has a face as gentle as a lotus or the moon; Māheśvarī is playful; Kaumārī destroys the pride of enemies; Vaiṣṇavī bears the discus as her weapon;
Vārāhī has a mouth with a deep, terrible, and rumbling sound; and Aindrī possesses the thunderbolt as her weapon.
May Cāmuṇḍā, Gaṇanātha, Bhairava, and the hosts of Mātṛkās protect me.
Seated upon the central triple throne, her face radiant with pride and joy, she is intensely luminous as Vajrapadmā;

on the petals of the eight directions, beginning with Brahmāṇī, reside the eight goddesses in the vowels and the syllable *praṇava* at the sacred sites such as Śrī-Prayāga; joined with the letters *va, sa, ṣa, sa, ha, kṣa*, they flash forth within the twenty-cornered [mandala] at the tip of the vajra.
May she who consists of thirty-two syllables—divided into three parts with twenty-eight [syllables] and accompanied by the stages of the sequence—protect us.
The sword, the accomplishment of mantras, the ruin of the foremost cities, flight through the sky, or the eye;
the paralyzing of enemies, victory surrounded by bees, the immobilization of all sciences;
long life, poetic talent, the treasure, the elixir, the pill, the sandals, and the accomplishment of desires.
All that is inconceivable is consumed by Alivali, joined with Bhairava and united with another.

I am dark-red in hue, three-eyed, burdened by the weight of my breasts, with the gait of an elephant in rut; I have lips like the *bimba* fruit, beautiful eyes, broad hips adorned with a girdle, and the splendor of jewels.
My limbs are graced by divine garments, and my mass of curly hair is as dark as a *valavala* flower.
May I be known as the illustrious Kubjikā, bestowing the unfailing, divine flood of the swift Command.
Resembling the luster of the Bandhuka flower, three-eyed, seated upon a lion-throne, beautiful,
the remover of all enemies here for everyone, adorned with white garments,
possessing eighteen pure lotus-hands that grant the fruits of one's desires— [I bow to her].
I bow to that Ambikā, the Mistress of Tumba, the destroyer of the demon Mahiṣāsura.
Where is the ether, where the wind, where the fire, where the waters,
where the earth, where Brahmā, where Janārdana, where the serpent, where Indra, and where the gods and asuras?
Delighted by the Lord of Yoga, Śrī Siddhi, who has been brought low by the warriors at the end of the aeon!
Victorious is the Lord Mahābhairava, the hero of the drama of play.
The Lord [is] Mahākāla, the Great Rudra, with the luster of black collyrium,
possessing a massive form and a great body, holding a curved knife and a skull-cup.
Homage be to you, O Mahākāla, the three-eyed deity with the brilliance of blazing fire, who wields the sword and the *pheṭaka* staff, and who is the destroyer of enemies.
He, who is devoted to the Brahmanas, performed an incarnation for the sake of bestowing grace upon those afflicted by calamity, until even Brahmā was reduced to powder by his hand.
May this splendor of the goddess Caṇḍikā— whose head is adorned with the severed, joyful [heads] of the Daityas and who is the essence of hymns— be forever the source of glory for the world.
The Goddess who is the destroyer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, who is the devourer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, who, as Māyā, brought about the destruction of the Asura Mahiṣa, and who is the consumer of Raktabīja;
she who is the crusher of the Daityas Śumbha and Niśumbha, and who is the Śrī of the God of Gods.
May that goddess protect me with her right arms, and may Jayā, O Caṇḍī, protect me.
Seated upon the pericarp of a full-blown lotus is the supreme Śrī Siddhilakṣmī,
white as camphor, crystal, and the moon-kunda flower; she is the remover of all bonds,
the unshakable boat for those drowning in the mud of suffering within the ocean of saṃsāra.
May she who possesses five glorious lotus-faces and ten arms, seated upon a corpse, protect you!
O fulfiller of hopes, remover of sins, destroyer of the flood of the world's suffering, deliverer from afflictions, slayer of enemies, ender of delusion in the world’s cycle of existence;
O source of splendor, O Cause, O best of gods, [salutations] to you who move through the pain of living beings!
Obeisance to you, Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, who instantly bestows the desired fruits upon the gods.
That which abides in the cavity of the fire of destruction in a radiant form, situated in the midst of the petals of the path of the moon, sun, and fire;
whose nature is the reality that is the cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution; and in whom all states of being—mind, consciousness, objects, and senses—are dissolved.
Consisting of gnosis, differentiated by the divisions of all phenomena,
gladdened by bliss, and eternally absorbed in the ultimate reality;
she is the channel whose form is composed of digits and who takes the nature of mantra.
It consists of seventeen syllables, with the letters *kha*, *la*, and *ucchi* excluded.
O hundred-syllable Vidyā, you who have reached the peak of fierce ritual actions, you who are perfected through union with the supreme family of the Lord of the Three Worlds;
you alone, though possessing manifold paths, are the most excellent wheel worthy of worship.
O you who are perfected through association with the virtuous and worshipped by Bhairava!
She whose waves of time are fashioned by the digits of Kālī, who flows as the vehicle [of consciousness], who dwells within the circles of the Śrīcakra and is undivided by any distinction,
who is full, joined with the moon, and possesses the form of the sun of the Kula.
The supreme accomplishment of consciousness is established in the Fire family.
Having attained the state of the sky-farer, she is supremely fierce;
she is the shore of the great meaning of the mantra proclaimed by Cakramenā.
Devoted to the yoga of the company of the virtuous, she bestows the accomplishments of the Kula.
I bow down to Kālī, who is supreme, natural, and inherent.
Bearing the splendor of Indra’s very bow upon her forehead, possessing the beauty of the sun, and spreading the white radiance of Gaurī on all sides—
this is that Tripurā, who, like the light of the sun in the heart, remains forever burning with brilliance.
May she, who consists of light and consists of speech, suddenly sever the garland of the destroyer of the three cities.
Māyā, Kuṇḍalinī, Kriyā, Madhumatī, Kālī, Kalāmālinī, Mātaṅgī, Vijayā, Jayā, Bhagavatī, Devī, Śivā, Sāmbhavī, Śakti,
the beloved of Śaṅkara, Trinayanī, Vāgvādinī, and Bhairavī.
Hrīṃ! You are Kālī, Tripurā, the supreme and non-supreme goddess, the Mother, and Kukārī.
Salutations to you, O Goddess of the lords of gods, Siddhilakṣmī of great splendor;
salutations to you, the Great Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, Rājyalakṣmī.
You are the supreme Kālī; you alone are Siddhilakṣmī.
You are Paracaṇḍī; you alone are Ugracaṇḍī.
You are the supreme Rājñī; you are the sovereign of the queens of kings.
May he, who has destroyed all [obstacles], bestow all perfections upon the virtuous person.
I speak of nothing else, nor do I hear, nor do I contemplate,
nor do I remember anything else; I worship none other, nor do I take refuge in any other, for I am liberated by my devoted service to your lotus feet.
Protect me, O Bhūti; out of compassion, grant me spiritual accomplishment.
Just as armor serves as a defense against the strikes of arrows,
even so may peace serve as a protection against the afflictions of the creator.

May the Kṣetrapāla of his own abode, together with Brahmāṇī and the others, along with Aśiṅga Bhairava, the Gaṇas, Vaṭukas, Yoginīs, and Kṣetrapālas, together with their limbs, retinues, and attendants, and the world-protectors such as Indra in the cardinal and intermediate directions, be well-pleased and grant boons. [The Statement]
In this rite of acceptance (*adhivāsana*) and worship of the sacrificial ground (*thaṇḍila*), for the sake of the specific purpose [of this ritual],

may there be the increase of longevity, health, sovereignty, food, wealth, fortune, progeny, and lineage for him and his circle of attendants; and may they become bestowers of the fruits as declared in the scriptures.
There is no other refuge; you alone are my refuge.
Therefore, O Supreme Goddess, protect me, protect me with your compassionate nature.
In this matter, regarding the worship consisting of perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, and the sacred thread,
may that entire ritual procedure of worship be completely fulfilled.
The libation.

Bhairava, who dwells upon the seat of the gratified departed spirits and removes the fear of worldly existence, and Caṇḍī, whose form is the mantra and who sits upon the fierce throne; the Gaṇas, Gurus, and Vaṭukas; the guardians of the world and their protectors;
the lords of serpents; the Rakṣasas and Yakṣas; the holy pilgrimage sites; the entire host of ancestors; and the Mothers.
May the Kṣetrapālas and Yoginīs, joined in yoga, drink this draught of that which moves in water and moves in the sky.
May the deities, the Rudras, and the Vināyakas, as well as the Yoginīs and Kṣetrapālas who are established within my body, drink [this].
Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Lord! Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Siddhinātha!
Oṃ, homage to the venerable Kujeśanātha; salutations again and again!
[The ritual procedure for honoring the sacrificial ground during the rite of formal acceptance is completed.]
